alerts.headline: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire agreement by year end 2026 moved up 8.8pp

topics.question: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire agreement by year end 2026

criteria_notes.manifold: Manifold asks "a ceasefire at any point in 2026", vs Polymarket's "agreement in force at year-end". Any-point-in-year is a broader window, yet Manifold sits lower — the gap is a criteria/venue difference to read, not a straight disagreement on likelihood.

topics.question: Will the Federal Reserve increase interest rates by the end of July 2026?
topics.explanation: The dominant driver is resolution-criteria mismatch, not genuine disagreement about Fed policy. Manifold covers any hike during all of 2026 and PredictIt extends to September 2026, giving the Fed many more opportunities to raise rates than Polymarket's market, which appears to focus specifically on the July 2026 FOMC meeting — a single decision point with a much lower probability of action. The ~44pp gap between Polymarket (~25%) and the other two (~62–68%) is almost entirely explained by this narrower time window, since a rate hike that doesn't occur in July could still occur in September or December and resolve Manifold/PredictIt YES but Polymarket NO.

criteria_notes.polymarket: Polymarket splits the July FOMC decision into one binary market per outcome bucket (no change / hike 25bp / hike 50bp / cut 25bp / cut 50bp) rather than a single "will they hike" market. The two hike buckets are summed here as mutually exclusive outcomes to get P(any increase) — verified live: ~24.05% + ~0.75% = ~24.8%.
criteria_notes.cme_fedwatch: CME FedWatch: real-money futures pricing of P(hike) at July 2026 FOMC meeting. This is the most liquid signal of Fed policy expectations.

topics.question: Republicans control the US Senate after the 2026 midterms

criteria_notes.manifold: Elections are the one theme traded on every venue at once, so this is the board's widest cross-source topic. Real-money venues (Polymarket, PredictIt) are correlation-damped together; Manifold is an independent play-money crowd.

topics.question: Will the CLARITY Act become law in 2026?
topics.explanation: The PredictIt market's notably higher probability (57%) likely reflects a different trader base and market structure — PredictIt attracts more casual/retail participants and has known pricing inefficiencies, and its question framing ("crypto regulation (Clarity Act)") may be interpreted more broadly to include any crypto market structure bill rather than specifically the CLARITY Act. Polymarket and Manifold, which skew toward more sophisticated prediction market participants, converge around 37-39%, suggesting genuine disagreement about legislative timeline rather than resolution criteria alone. The ~20pp spread is partially a resolution-criteria mismatch (what counts as "the CLARITY Act" vs. comparable legislation) and partially reflects differing assessments of Congressional capacity to advance crypto legislation through both chambers before year-end 2026.

topics.question: Will there be a new Romanian Prime Minister by end of September 2026?
Will a World War 3 scale global conflict occur by 2030?
topics.explanation: The two sources are measuring fundamentally different things, making this primarily a resolution-criteria mismatch rather than genuine disagreement. Polymarket's NATO-Russia military clash market captures a much lower escalation threshold (any direct military confrontation) over a shorter timeframe (by end 2026), which naturally yields a higher probability than an event requiring the full "World War 3 with nuclear weapons" threshold that Manifold's market implies. The remaining gap reflects that Polymarket traders price meaningful conventional clash risk while Manifold traders discount the additional steps required to go from clash → world war → nuclear use as compounding low-probability hurdles.

criteria_notes.polymarket: Reframed from the original "blockade or quarantine" question: no liquid blockade-specific market exists. This market resolves on an invasion / military offensive, which is a strictly higher bar than interdiction. Read the level, not the label.
criteria_notes.manifold: Manifold asks "attempt to invade by end of 2027" — an attempt is a slightly lower bar than Polymarket's "commences an offensive", so expect it to sit marginally higher.

criteria_notes.polymarket: The market resolves on any trade at/above $100k; the Yahoo oracle checks daily closes, so a brief intraday spike that does not close above $100k would not auto-resolve YES. Close enough to track together.
